scope: Proposition 3.6 (Radial spectral gap) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On the subspace of H generated by even, quarter-turn invariant spin tests, the spectrum of D below 3 consists of the constant state at 0 and one nonzero one-dimensional state at 1. There is a real linear functional ℓ with |ℓ(F)| ≤ ∥F∥2 such that, for real even quarter-turn invariant tests F, G of finite ordinary L2 norm and 0 < r ≤ 1, |E[(ΘF)D− log rG] − EFEG − rℓ(F)ℓ(G)| ≤ r3 ∥F∥2∥G∥2. (3.31) The assertion extends from smeared polynomials to bounded field tests by ordinary L2 approximation.
